title: Benchmark core Zedu workflows on low-end Android and slow networks
description: Measure the time, failures and data transferred for joining a workspace, following a cohort channel, joining a Buzz call and opening shared files on a representative low-end Android device under documented network conditions. Use a test account and test content. Record device, OS, network, sample size and limitations, then recommend the highest-impact improvements without promising unsupported offline behavior.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Define the pass/fail bar before measuring: per-journey time, data and failure budgets, so the benchmark numbers are actionable
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The accepted workstream runs the four-journey benchmark; without thresholds, its numbers cannot be acted on - nobody can say whether 9 MB for joining a workspace is good or bad. This idea defines the bar first. Approach: for each of the four journeys (joining a workspace, following a cohort channel, joining a Buzz call, opening shared files), set a documented pass/fail budget: a completion-time ceiling, a data-transferred ceiling per journey on the documented network profile, and a failure taxonomy (blocked, slow-but-working, data-heavy) with examples. Sources for the ceilings: the goal's own device and network assumptions, Zedu's low-data positioning on zedu.chat, and comparable messaging-app baselines, each cited - nothing invented. Then map the benchmark results onto pass/fail per journey with the rationale attached. Done when: each journey has a written threshold with its source, and every measured journey is graded pass or fail against it. Measured: four threshold sheets, four graded journeys, and a short note on which threshold is most often failed. Why this fits: it converts a measurement exercise into a release decision without duplicating the benchmark itself.

upvotes.reason: "Define the pass/fail bar before measuring: per-journey time, data and failure budgets, so the benchmark numbers are actionable" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Run a controlled four-journey mobile benchmark with repeatable network profiles
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Confirm the test device and environment first, then use the same synthetic account and content to run workspace joining, channel following, Buzz joining and shared-file opening under documented network profiles. Repeat each run consistently and record completion, elapsed time, transferred data and failures alongside device, OS and network settings. Deliver raw notes, a comparison table and prioritized causes only where evidence supports them; record unavailable conditions rather than inventing measurements.

upvotes.reason: "Run a controlled four-journey mobile benchmark with repeatable network profiles" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

pendingIdeas.title: Benchmark the same journeys against WhatsApp and Telegram on the same device and network
pendingIdeas.description: A number in isolation cannot change a decision; a comparison can. Work: run the equivalent actions in the app the cohort uses today (join a group, send a message, join a call, open a shared file) on the same device and network, and record time, data and failure for each. Deliver the side-by-side table, the note on where the comparison is unfair because the products differ, and the honest sentence about which journeys Zedu wins and which it loses on this hardware.

upvotes.reason: A Zedu-only number cannot tell a school whether it is slow relative to what teachers already use; comparing the same device and network makes the result decision-relevant.
A load time means nothing without a comparison. Running the same four journeys on the same device and network makes the result a decision input.

pendingIdeas.title: Measure the cold-start path separately from the warm one, because the first join is the expensive one
pendingIdeas.description: A benchmark that starts from an installed, signed-in app measures the easy case. A teacher's first session includes the download, the install, the sign-up, the workspace join and the first channel open, often on a phone with little free storage. Work: time each of those steps on the target device with the network profile documented, record where it fails and what the app asks the user to do about it. Deliver the cold-start timeline, the data cost of the install, and the single step that loses the most people.

upvotes.reason: First-session cost is the barrier; measuring a warm, signed-in app understates what a new teacher experiences.
The first join is the expensive path and the one a teacher experiences. Measuring download, install, sign-up and first channel open separately is the honest baseline.

A benchmark that starts from an installed, signed-in app measures the easy case. A teacher's first session includes download, install, sign-up, workspace join and first channel open, so timing those separately is what makes the benchmark usable for a decision.

pendingIdeas.title: Measure the first barrier too: app download size, storage needed and the data used on first sign-in
pendingIdeas.description: The accepted workstreams measure four journeys after the app is installed. On a low-end phone with paid data, the first barrier is installing and signing in. Approach: record the install size from the Play Store listing and on device, the free storage needed, and the data used from first launch through sign-in and the first workspace load (same device and network profiles as the benchmark). Compare it with the web app in a mobile browser as the no-install alternative. Done: an install-and-first-run table with method and limits, and a note on whether the web route is lighter for first-time learners.

upvotes.reason: "Measure the first barrier too: app download size, storage needed and the data used on first sign-in" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.

pendingIdeas.title: Record what the app does when the network fails, not only how long the happy path takes
pendingIdeas.description: On a 2G connection the interesting number is not the average load time, it is what happens on timeout: does the app retry forever, send a message twice, lose a typed draft, or show a spinner with no message. Work: with the network profile dropping packets and cutting out mid-action, exercise send, upload, join call and open file, and record the visible outcome and the retry behaviour. Deliver the failure table, the duplicates or losses observed, and the three fixes with the highest effect per unit of work.

upvotes.reason: On 2G the timeout behaviour matters more than the average load; recording what the app does when the connection fails is the actionable number.
On a weak connection the timeout behaviour matters more than the average. Recording retries, duplicate sends and lost drafts is the useful evidence.

pendingIdeas.title: Test a mid-call network drop, because a dropped Buzz session is the failure educators talk about
pendingIdeas.description: The four journeys include joining a call, but the reported pain is usually a call that dies and does not come back. Work: start a two-participant call, cut the network for ten, thirty and sixty seconds, then restore it; record whether audio returns, whether the app says anything, whether the user must rejoin, and what the other participant sees. Deliver the recovery table per outage length, the user-facing message that is missing, and the recommendation on whether to retry automatically or tell the user plainly.

upvotes.reason: A Buzz call that dies and cannot be rejoined is the failure educators describe; testing the drop path is more useful than a clean join time.
A dropped Buzz session is the failure teachers remember. Testing ten, thirty and sixty-second network cuts and whether audio returns is the right scenario.

A call that dies and does not come back is the failure educators actually report, and the accepted workstream only covers joining one. Testing ten, thirty and sixty second drops gives a recovery table instead of an average that hides the problem.

pendingIdeas.title: Turn the measured data cost into a monthly naira figure a school can compare with its data bundle
pendingIdeas.description: Megabytes mean nothing to a bursar; a monthly cost against a data plan does. Work: from the measured bytes per session for the four journeys, compute a monthly figure for three usage patterns (a learner joining two classes a week, a teacher running a daily session, an organiser uploading files) at a published Nigerian data price, with the assumption stated. Deliver the cost table, the comparison with a WhatsApp call of the same length, and the sentence a salesperson can use without overclaiming.

upvotes.reason: A bursar compares money, not megabytes; converting measured data use into a monthly naira figure makes the benchmark usable.
Megabytes do not change a bursar's mind; a monthly naira figure against a data plan does. Turning measurements into that number makes the benchmark usable.
